author: Bruno Mulé
title: Francisco Lindor homers for Mets lone run
desc: Francisco Lindor supplied the Mets' only run Monday against the Blue Jays with a solo home run. He pulled a Trey Yesavage fastball 378 feet to right field for his third homer of the season and first in four games since returning from the injured list.
impact: The homer was Lindor's only hit, though he also produced a 100 mph flyout and a 98 mph lineout in the contest.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Sean Manaea allows two runs in loss
desc: Sean Manaea took the loss Monday against the Blue Jays after allowing two runs on three hits and two walks over 5.2 innings. He struck out four and finished one out shy of recording his second quality start of the season.
impact: Manaea has posted a 4.05 ERA, 1.20 WHIP, and 19:5 K across 20 innings as a starter, compared to a 5.02 ERA and 1.44 WHIP over 44 relief innings. He is scheduled to finish his two-start week this weekend in Atlanta.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Jacob Latz records six-out save
desc: Jacob Latz earned the save Monday against Cleveland after retiring all six batters he faced over two scoreless innings. He struck out one and did not allow a hit or walk while securing his 17th save of the season.
impact: Latz owns a 1.76 ERA, 0.63 WHIP, and 41:9 K across 41 innings. He has posted scoreless outings in 11 of his last 12 appearances and has not blown a save since May 13.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Chris Paddack works four innings in Rangers debut
desc: Chris Paddack allowed two runs on seven hits with no walks and one strikeout over four innings of bulk relief in Monday's win over the Guardians. He worked three scoreless frames before giving up both runs in his final inning after signing with Texas earlier in the day.
impact: Paddack entered his Rangers debut with an 0-7 record, 6.96 ERA, 1.66 WHIP, and 39:19 K across 53 innings between Miami and Cincinnati. His role with Texas remains unclear, and he will need better results before regaining fantasy relevance if he moves into the rotation.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Anthony Seigler extends hitting streak to seven games
desc: Anthony Seigler started at second base and went 2-for-3 with a stolen base and a run scored in Monday's 6-3 win over the Nationals. He made his seventh consecutive start and has recorded at least one hit in each game.
impact: Seigler is 11-for-23 with three doubles, one home run, three RBI, one stolen base, and five runs during the seven-game streak. Injuries to Trevor Story and Marcelo Mayer have created additional playing time in Boston's infield.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Caleb Durbin launches seventh homer
desc: Caleb Durbin went 1-for-3 with a solo home run and a walk in Monday's 6-3 win over the Nationals. He sent a hanging sweeper over the Green Monster in the first inning to extend Boston's early lead.
impact: Durbin is slashing .325/.360/.614 with six home runs, 13 RBI, 16 runs, and five stolen bases across 24 games in June. He is batting .231/.286/.393 with seven homers, 35 RBI, 31 runs, and nine steals through 76 games this season.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Willson Contreras homers before ejection
desc: Willson Contreras went 1-for-2 with a three-run home run in Monday's 6-3 win over the Nationals. He launched a 421-foot shot over the Green Monster in the first inning before being ejected by first-base umpire Nic Lentz following a strikeout in the second. Andruw Monasterio replaced him at first base.
impact: Contreras is slashing .282/.376/.533 with 18 home runs, 53 RBI, 41 runs, and one stolen base across 81 games this season.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Garrett Whitlock records first save
desc: Garrett Whitlock earned his first save of the season Monday against the Nationals, allowing one hit and no walks while striking out two in a scoreless ninth inning. He handled closing duties with Aroldis Chapman unavailable after pitching on each of the previous two days.
impact: Whitlock has allowed one run over eight innings with a 7:0 K since returning from the injured list June 9. He owns a 2.60 ERA, 1.05 WHIP, and 32:6 K across 27.2 innings, though regular save opportunities are unlikely while Chapman remains Boston's closer.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Ranger Suarez strikes out eight in fourth win
desc: Ranger Suarez earned the win Monday against the Nationals after allowing three runs on five hits and one walk over six innings. He struck out eight while recording a quality start in Boston's 6-3 victory. Suarez surrendered a leadoff homer to James Wood and later allowed a two-run double to CJ Abrams in the sixth inning.
impact: Suarez finished June with a 2.10 ERA, 1.07 WHIP, and 35:7 K across 30 innings and five starts. He owns a 2.94 ERA, 1.13 WHIP, and 92:26 K through 104 innings, with his next outing tentatively scheduled for Sunday against the Angels.

author: Jesse Garcia
title: Miles Mikolas gets tagged for six in seven vs. Boston
desc: Miles Mikolas allowed six earned runs on nine hits and no walks while striking out three over seven innings in Monday's loss to the Red Sox.
impact: After the defeat, he now owns a 5.44 ERA and 1.29 WHIP with a 2-7 record across 18 games. Mikolas was able to eat some innings for the Nationals despite falling behind 4-0 after the first inning. He will look to bounce back in his next outing, scheduled to take place against the Pirates.

author: Jesse Garcia
title: James Wood flashes power in 6-3 loss to Boston
desc: James Wood went 1-for-4 in a loss to the Red Sox with a home run, a run scored, one RBI and two strikeouts.
impact: After Monday's loss, Wood is batting .258 with 21 home runs, 50 RBI, 73 runs scored and 13 stolen bases across 86 games, along with a .378 wOBA. Wood's bat has gone quiet as of late, as he is just 3-for-30 in his last seven games with 16 strikeouts.

author: Jesse Garcia
title: Shane Baz grinds through seven
desc: Shane Baz fought the zone but mostly kept the damage contained, though the lack of efficiency and run support led to a no-decision.
impact: Shane Baz allowed two earned runs on four hits and four walks while striking out six over seven innings in Monday's loss to the White Sox. After the outing, Baz now has a 4.19 ERA and 1.37 WHIP with a 4-8 record, 7.8 K/9 and a 2.23 K:BB across 17 starts.

author: Jesse Garcia
title: Colton Cowser's patience didn't save a quiet night against Chicago
desc: Colton Cowser went 0-for-2 in loss to the White Sox with two walks, two strikeouts and one stolen base.
impact: After Monday's loss, Cowser is batting .232 with eight home runs, 27 RBI, 27 runs scored and four stolen bases across 75 games. Cowser is just 3-for-17 in his last seven games.

author: Matthew Adam
title: Gabriel Arias Pops Solo Shot, But Guardians Fall Short
desc: Gabriel Arias went 1-for-3 in Monday's 6-3 loss to the Rangers with a home run, a run scored and one RBI.
impact: Arias launched a solo shot in the fifth inning to tie the game at 1-1. Through 20 games, he's batting .217 with three homers, six RBI, four runs scored and a 26:2 K:BB (41.3% strikeout rate) across 60 at-bats.

author: Matthew Adam
title: Brayan Rocchio swipes a bag in loss
desc: Brayan Rocchio went 2-for-5 in a 6-3 loss to the Rangers with a run scored and a stolen base.
impact: Rocchio continues to provide solid fantasy production. After Monday's loss to Texas, Rocchio is slashing .271/.343/.386 with five home runs, 34 RBI, 33 runs scored, and 14 stolen bases across 82 games. He's hitting .290 with two steals over his past seven games.
